why: testcode/202609051531 is the arrival the architect identified as smooth. It is pinned here as the ORACLE: the build every candidate Atlas is measured against. An oracle is not an opinion about design - it is a set of numbers a candidate must not be worse than.

oracle.bound_how: the REPD identity shards under atlas/data/repd-identities were first cut at 202609051214, after 202609051156 shipped, and the record for REPD 11386 matches that spine on name, technology, capacity_mw, longitude, latitude and county
oracle.map_button: testcode/202609051531/capsule-launch.js builds new URL('./atlas/', location.href) - the Atlas is RELATIVE to the release, so PipelineNews and the Atlas ship together on one origin under one timestamp

baseline.note: Medians of three runs per lane, Playwright chromium, iPhone 14 Pro profile for mobile and 1440x900 for desktop. A single sample is a number, not a baseline.

engine_must_fire_every_run.why: The card stating 'Nearest <n> kV substation:' is the only evidence the grid engine ran. A project name on screen proves the card was built, nothing more - that conflation is what let an earlier harness report 94/94 while the map was still being complained about.

mobile_declared_kb.why: The oracle reads ONE ~120 KB REPD identity shard keyed by the ref's prefix. The live Atlas downloads a parquet dataset plus the duckdb WASM extension, measured at 17,021 KB against the oracle's 7,059 KB on the same arrival. On a phone that is the difference the architect can feel.

engine_ms.why: Time to the engine's answer, not time to first paint. A build may load quickly and still leave the reader without the number they came for. The bound is 1.6x, not tighter: re-measuring the ORACLE against its own baseline produced 1,797 ms on mobile against a 1,207 ms median, so a live network moves this by half again on its own. A gate that fails the build it was written from is measuring jitter, not regression - this is here to catch a structural change, and payload and drawn features are the axes that hold still.

rendered_features.why: What is actually DRAWN on arrival. The oracle renders 180; the live Atlas renders 62-74 on the same arrival. Equal layer counts hid this - both carry 194 style layers - so counting layers is not the check.

l_subs_visible_on_arrival.why: Arriving from a project must show the substations the card measures to. Asserted directly rather than inferred from a screenshot, because a backgrounded tab stalls MapLibre and makes a working map look blank.

repd_lookup_is_sharded.why: A bulk parquet fetch on every arrival is the cause of the mobile payload gap, not a symptom of it. Naming the cause means a candidate cannot pass by trimming something else. Matched on the DATASET - parquet files, partitioned masters, whole-register payloads - never on the duckdb library, which the oracle also loads.
